correctness.rationale: The graph \(L(Q_3)\) is defined unambiguously by twelve binary cube edges; both complete implementations evaluate exactly \(3^{12}=531{,}441\) states, and their integer maps agree on all temporal counts. The C++ functional graph algorithm proves the complete period and entry census by exhaustive indegree pruning; the Python implementation separately checks \(F^{22}=F^{10}\), a witness at depth 10, exact fixed powers, full entry layers, and the automorphism-orbit histogram. The maximal triangular-clique reconstruction proves that all 48 spatial graph automorphisms are considered. The proof and code have no unverified extrapolation.

value.rationale: The cuboctahedral graph \(L(Q_3)\) is a canonical twelve-vertex quartic Archimedean graph, not an arbitrarily selected labelled instance. Its coexistence of triangular and square face/neighbor structures motivates comparing three- and four-step excitable waves. The exact four-class octahedral period-four splitting reveals distinct spatial waves even where aggregate four-step spike counts coincide, and the full entrance-time census with sharp cutoff provides a natural reproducible reference for finite excitation systems. Such an exact natural finite invariant is not implied by the cited general theory, without claiming an infinite-family result.
